notes: §1985:VI.3.3.4 GR1: "The program-name identifies the source program, the object program, and all listings pertaining to a particular program." BinderDriver.MakeUnit reads the PROGRAM-ID paragraph's program-name as the unit's Name, derives the emitted class name from it and sets ExternalizedName to the same word; the only way the two differ, the AS literal-1 phrase of 2002, is refused at --std 85 by VersionConformancePass.VisitExternalizedNamePhrase (Constructs.ExternalizedNameAs2002, COBOL0900, probed), so at 85 the object program carries the program-name alone. ProgramEmitter.EmitModuleRegistrar and HostEntryEmitter.EmitEntry emit that name into ProgramRegistry.Register and the unit's repository record, and a CALL finds the program by it. Probed at 85: three programs in one source, called by literal in either case and by identifier (PGM-ID-1, SUB-A, 9sub-b), each run; a name no program has takes ON OVERFLOW; two programs of one name in a sequence are refused (COBOL2213); a literal for the program-name does not parse. The compiler writes no listing (the CLI has no listing option), so the listings clause has nothing to name; diagnostics carry the source file and line. The witness calls two separately compiled programs of one source by their program-names.

next.reason: 1985: "The program-name identifies the source program, the object program, and all listings pertaining to a particular program."; 2023: "Literal-1, if specified, is the name of the program that is externalized to the operating environment.". 2023 adds literal-1, so the externalized (object) name can differ from program-name-1. It also drops the statement that program-name identifies the listings.
